jobs.description:
Moment Professionals is recruiting on behalf of FPRT a Strategic Projects & Business Operations Manager based in Vojens, Denmark. We are looking for a project manager with a consultant's or project developer's mindset, who takes ownership of cross-functional business projects, takes the first step in understanding and structuring an issue and brings the CEO clear recommendations. The role suits you if you want to build structure in a company that is being built right now, with pragmatic, lightweight project management appropriate for a greenfield environment.

Your everyday at FPRT

You report to the CEO and take over the project management of FPRT's business and corporate projects, which the CHRO carries today alongside HR. The role has no direct reports to begin with, and you work across most of the company, with the Chief Production Officer, the process engineers, production, data, finance, HR and supply chain, as well as external implementation partners and advisers. The CEO communicates briefly and precisely, often on chat, takes challenge well and builds the collaboration on trust. Your mandate grows as that trust grows.

In the first months the SAP implementation is the largest task. An external partner implements the system, and you are FPRT's internal business project lead for the implementation: you keep track of progress and next steps, translate operational needs into clear requirements together with the functional owners and drive the solution into daily use across production planning, stock management, logistics and the integration of the systems FPRT selects in this period. Next come warehouse and logistics, selected governance and cross-functional operating processes, and business cases, for example for a new factory. Along the way you coordinate grant applications, public funding submissions and bank and investor material with internal owners and external partners.

You take the first step in understanding and structuring an issue, identify what information and expertise are needed, and then involve the right people. When a financing partner sends a long list of questions with a 48-hour deadline, you draft the answers from the documents that exist, mark how certain each answer is and bring them to the CEO and the right colleagues for a short validation. You prepare decisions as options, risks, advantages and price on one page with a clear recommendation, and you escalate delays and unresolved risks with a recommendation of your own.

The role is based in Vojens. You have the flexibility to work from home when a task needs focus, and in intense project periods you are on site every day, sometimes for a month or more. English is used a lot in daily work, and Danish is preferred, since FPRT is building a company in Denmark. If your Danish is not fluent yet, the right competencies count most.

And then there are the benefits:

A central role close to the CEO with direct influence on how a new company is built, ownership of business systems, processes, funding and business cases from day one, a mandate that grows with the trust you build, a culture where challenge with facts is welcome, and flexibility to work from home when focus requires it.

To succeed in the role…

…you do not need to have carried the title project manager or to come from defence. What matters is that you take ownership of cross-functional business projects, structure an issue before you involve the right people, and give a firm recommendation with the reasoning behind it. You also take pride in:

• 
challenging the CEO and colleagues with arguments and keeping the dialogue constructive.

• 
finding the information yourself and knowing when to escalate.

• 
keeping project management agile, with the minimum structure that makes it work.

• 
working with a risk until it is reduced, once you have identified it.

• 
involving busy colleagues firmly and kindly, so they like working with you.

What you need to bring:

• 
Either a relevant degree in business administration, finance, economics, engineering management or a related field, or equivalent experience, and at least five years of relevant experience or a strong track record of cross-functional business projects.

• 
Basic project management skills, including stakeholder management and risk assessment, gained through education or practice.

• 
Experience as business project lead or coordinator on an ERP or other business-system implementation. Method and implementation experience matter more than specialist system knowledge.

• 
Executive-level communication in English, written and spoken: short, clear and decision-oriented.

• 
The possibility to be on site in Vojens every day in intense periods.

It is an advantage if you:

• 
come from management consulting or advisory, for example an audit and advisory firm such as the Big 4, or from business transformation, corporate development or strategy and operations in a scale-up.

• 
have worked with grant applications, public funding, or bank and investor material.

• 
have prepared business cases and cost-benefit analyses for executive decisions.

• 
speak Danish.

Do you want to join the team at FPRT?

Moment Professionals manages the recruitment process on behalf of FPRT. We review applications continuously and close the process when the right candidate has been found.

The process may include interviews with Moment Professionals and FPRT, a case, relevant tests and reference checks.

Due to the sensitive defense-tech nature of FPRT's projects and operations, all potential employees are subject to a police and intelligence background check as part of FPRT's standard recruitment process. Continued employment is conditional upon obtaining and maintaining the necessary security clearance.

If you are interested, you are very welcome to apply via the application link, and we will assess your application as soon as possible. If you have questions that can help you decide whether the position is right for you, you are welcome to contact Moment Professionals by phone on +45 70 20 18 35 or by email at info@moment.dk. All enquiries are treated confidentially.

The company

FirePoint Rocket Technology (FPRT) is building one of the most unique and strategically important industrial projects in Denmark: a new production facility for solid rocket propellant and advanced defense-tech components. FPRT's ambition is significant: the company is scaling from the early operational phase to 300+ employees within the next 18 months. Joining FPRT now means becoming part of the core team shaping a new high-tech, safety-critical production environment from the ground up.

Are you a software or computer science student who wants to apply what you learn to real projects in an industry moving full speed ahead with digitalisation? Do you want to work on the tools that help us run a more efficient and greener fleet? If you have an interest in maritime shipping and want to be part of its transformation, we’d love to hear from you!

What you will do...

As our new Student Assistant working out of our Copenhagen office, you will join the Fleet Efficiency & Decarbonisation team. You will help build and maintain the team’s internal data and web applications: Python back-end, PostgreSQL database, web front-end and automated tests, AI assistants, deployed on Microsoft Azure. Your tasks are matched to your experience and your study schedule.

Among other interesting tasks, you will:

• Develop, test, and maintain internal tools and applications that support fleet performance and decarbonisation

• Build and improve back-end services and REST APIs in Python

• Write SQL queries, database migrations and data checks in PostgreSQL

• Improve the web front-end and the user experience

• Ensure code quality, maintainability, and portability

• Collaborate closely with domain experts and fellow developers

We offer a flexible working week of 2-3 days, with more hours required during holiday periods and fewer hours during your exam periods.

We’re looking for a team player who…

• Has a strong sense of ownership and responsibility

• Thrives in a collaborative environment but works independently with confidence

• Embraces constructive feedback and continuously seeks growth as a developer

• Communicates ideas clearly and effectively

• Understands user needs and perspectives

We furthermore expect that you…

• Are enrolled in a bachelor’s or master’s programme in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field, with at least one year of studies left

• Have solid programming skills in Python

• Have working knowledge of SQL and relational databases (e.g. PostgreSQL, MSSQL)

• Are familiar with web development (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) and REST APIs

• Have experience with version control (Git) and a collaborative workflow

• Ideally, but not necessarily, have worked with a Python web framework (e.g. FastAPI, Django), Docker, or a cloud platform (e.g. Azure)

• Are interested in learning AI / LLM APIs

• Are fluent in English (written and spoken), as this is our corporate language. Danish is not a requirement.

• Hold a permit allowing you to live and work onsite in Denmark.

Not meeting every single bullet above? We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. If you're excited about this role but your experience doesn't exactly match all the qualifications in the job description, we still encourage you to apply.

What you might love about us

We have a strong youth community with trainees, interns and student assistants. With more than 30 nationalities across 10 locations, you will step into a genuinely international, informal and social environment: the kind where people enjoy working together, not just working next to each other. In Ultrabulk, we are convinced that an optimal working environment requires an exceptional social atmosphere across all departments. We believe that work should be fun and rewarding on a personal level. Our mission to be ‘a partner you can trust’ shines through in our way of being colleagues by caring for one another and, in unison, do our utmost to reach our goals for the business. We believe that flexibility is fundamental in ensuring a balanced life.

Application

We would like you to start as soon as possible. If you would like to learn more about the position, please reach out to Harshit Tripathi, Head of Fleet Efficiency & Decarbonisation at harshit.tripathi@ultrabulk.com.

Ready to set sail on this exciting journey with us? We encourage you to apply as soon as possible, as applications are evaluated continuously, and interviews will take place on an ongoing basis. The deadline for uploading your CV and application is 22 November 2026, but we will close the position once the ideal match for our team has been found. Only applications uploaded digitally will be taken into consideration; we do not accept applications sent via e-mail. Your application will be treated with confidentiality and our reply will be sent to the e-mail address you have registered in our recruitment system.

We are committed to providing an inclusive and supportive recruitment experience for all candidates. If you have any specific needs, please let us know how we can assist.

The recruitment process

In Ultra, our recruitment philosophy is simple. For each and every job to be filled we are looking for the strongest talents out there.

We invest our time and resources in finding the right match in terms of competencies, experience, personality and culture - just as the candidate is investing his or her energy to evaluate us as a prospective employer.

Therefore, we are meticulous and consistent with the process of hiring a new colleague for our teams.

About Ultrabulk

Ultrabulk is a leading global dry bulk operator, offering a broad range of shipping services to accommodate our customers in their maritime transportation needs in the Panamax, Supramax and Handysize segments as well as with our Specialised Services. Ultrabulk operates a fleet of 160 to 190 vessels managed by a professional team, strategically located at 10 offices worldwide (Copenhagen, Cape Town, Dubai, New York, Rio de Janeiro, Santiago, Shanghai, Singapore, Sydney and Tokyo).

Ready to take the next step in your Risk Management career?

Do you have a natural flair for numbers and strong analytical skills? Are you ready to develop your commercial understanding of the dynamic fuel and shipping industry that facilitates global trade? As an in-house Risk Management Analyst, you will help our customers mitigate risks and navigate uncertainty and volatility. Strong relationships and stakeholder management will be central to how you create that value.

Job description

Monjasa is a leading global partner in the oil and shipping industry who believes strongly in driving Personal Business. We aim to inspire our business partners and become first choice by challenging status quo with our original solutions. We are on the lookout to expand the Risk Management team with a colleague who can identify with Monjasa’s values and can build strong relations both internally and externally.

In this role, you will work closely with Trading to propose fixed forward prices for physical bunker sales. You will define the hedging requirements and coordinate with our Derivatives team to manage the associated risk. The Derivatives team executes the paper hedges.

You will be based at our office in Fredericia and report directly to the Group Treasury and Risk Management Senior Manager. During onboarding, you will spend time with your team at our Hellerup office to build your functional knowledge and relationships. For approximately two months, you can expect three travel days to Hellerup per week.

Your role will develop quickly: you will first learn about our business activities and products, the mechanics of risk management, and pricing and hedging on live deals. As you build this foundation, you will progress towards more independent responsibility for quoting, hedge coordination and post-trade follow-up.

What you will be doing

• Act as the go-to person for traders on fixed vs. floating pricing requests, with fast and accurate turnaround

• Work side by side with other Risk Management colleagues to provide Trading with fixed forward prices

• Identify and mitigate risks inherent with fixed forward prices

• Define the hedging requirements for each deal, including the index, volume and tenor, and coordinate with the Derivatives team, which executes the paper trades

• Monitor basis risk—the risk arising from differences between physical pricing and the paper index—and flag when hedges no longer match the physical position

• Follow physical liftings, delivery shifts and volume changes, and propose the resulting hedge adjustments or unwinds

• Track PnL against realized outcome, and give feedback on pricing accuracy after delivery

• Analyze forward curves, spreads and volatility to provide insights with Global Trading teams

• Build and maintain pricing and risk tools in Excel and dashboards, and contribute to ad-hoc projects on pricing policy and process improvement

What we are looking for

Professional skills

• Degree in Finance, Economics, Engineering, Mathematics or another quantitative discipline

• Understanding of the commodity or energy markets with a few years of relevant experience

• Knowledge of swaps, futures and forward curves in relation to physical pricing, together with experience in a bank or financial institution focused on paper trading, is an advantage

• High proficiency in Excel and AI tools

• Fluency in both written and verbal English

Personal skills - We are looking for someone who can:

• Organize your own tasks, check the details and stay focused when deadlines are tight

• Ask questions, explore unfamiliar topics and put what you learn into practice

• Use data and facts to question assumptions and challenge decisions

• Take ownership and communicate complex risk clearly and with confidence to both internal and external stakeholders

• Build strong working relationships across functions, collaborating with internal stakeholders in commercial and back-office teams as well as external customers

What we offer

At Monjasa, Personal Business is about the relationships we build together. You will join an international working environment where respect, ambition, curiosity and smile & joy shape everyday life. With hands-on learning, mentoring, relevant courses and regular development conversations, you will have opportunities to grow both professionally and personally. At our Fredericia office, shared lunches, fitness facilities and social events create space to connect beyond daily tasks. You can expect a working life centered on learning, strong relationships and a sense of belonging. That’s how we see life at Monjasa - but we would love for you to experience it yourself.

Questions?

Cecilie Holm

HR Specialist

Contact Cecilie

E-mail: hr.eur@monjasa.com

Phone: +45 76 317 392

We look forward to receiving your application no later than 26 November 2026. In the meantime, we encourage you to take a look into Monjasa and read more about the company here.

Please contact HR support on this email: hr.eur@monjasa.com

Monjasa as a workplace

Monjasa offers you a fulfilling career in a global organisation, where you will be part of a dynamic and ambitious team. We enjoy great learning opportunities and are proud of our fantastic working environment.

We are driven by our values of Respect, Ambition, Curiosity and Smile & Joy and by our corporate purpose of making our business personal and challenging the status quo. Among our colleagues, you will find more than 50 different nationalities, and we pride ourselves on being a diverse workplace with people of different backgrounds and beliefs. We truly believe that an inclusive workplace leads to a healthy working environment, where we are all onboard and thriving as a team.

Monjasa at a glance

Monjasa is a global partner in the oil and shipping industries and among the world’s top 10 largest marine fuel suppliers. Our core business includes trading and supplying marine fuels and shipowning activities globally.

We are characterised by a strong entrepreneurial spirit and have experienced strong developments since our start in 2002.  Today, the Monjasa Group employs more than 700 traders, seafarers and other maritime specialists.

With a fleet of some 30 vessels and 15 office locations in Europe, the Americas, the Middle East & Africa and Asia, we are a close shipping partner in more than 800 ports worldwide.

Monjasa Group revenue reached a total of USD 4bn in 2025.

**Why we are hiring

**Spirii is growing. We work with charge point operators, businesses and fleets in several European markets, we take part in more and more tenders, and our commercial team has grown along the way. With growth comes friction. Deals and tenders are tracked in different places, the numbers in the CRM do not always match what we bill, and it takes too much effort to answer simple questions like “what will we close this quarter?”

We want one person to own the engine behind our revenue: the CRM, the data, and the path a customer takes from first contact to signed deal, onboarding and correct billing. That is this role. You will make work easier for our sales, marketing, onboarding and customer success teams, and you will give leadership numbers they can trust.

**The team

**You will report to our CSO. You will own Revenue Operations from end to end, and you will work every day with sales development, account executives, marketing, onboarding and customer success, and closely with Finance on billing data.

**What You Will Do

****CRM and tools

**

• Own and improve HubSpot, our CRM, so everyone works from the same clean data

• Make sure every deal and tender is tracked in one place, from first contact to result

• Set up and improve lead routing

• Bring in the other tools the commercial team needs, such as order management, bid management and lead development

• Make sure master data is correct, so billing runs smoothly

**Metrics and forecasting

**

• Define and track our core SaaS metrics: ARR, ACV, TCV, NRR and pipeline stages

• Run the weekly forecast and track how accurate it is

• Connect marketing, sales development, account executives and customer success, so the forecast reflects what is really happening

**Data and reporting

**

• Build dashboards that leadership trusts and uses to make decisions

• Keep the CRM clean and reconcile it with billing data

**Planning and sales process

**

• Build one clear sales process, with the same stages and rules from lead to handover across teams and markets

• Support territory design and regional planning reviews

• Run capacity modelling and lead quota planning

• Improve the path from lead to opportunity

**What Success Looks Like After Your First Year

**

• Leadership opens one dashboard and trusts what it sees

• Every deal and tender lives in HubSpot, and CRM data matches billing data

• The weekly forecast is a habit, and it gets more accurate over time

• Every market follows the same sales process

• Our sales team spends less time on admin and more time with customers

**What You Bring

**

• 5+ years in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations or commercial analytics in a B2B SaaS company

• Strong CRM administration skills, ideally in HubSpot

• A track record of building tools and processes that help a sales organisation work better

• Comfort with data: Excel, SQL, or BI tools such as Tableau

• A good understanding of SaaS business models and unit economics

• Hands-on experience bringing AI tools into a sales or marketing team

• Fluent English. Another European language, such as German, French, Dutch, Swedish, Danish or Italian, is a big plus

• A degree in business, engineering or a similar field, or equivalent experience

**Who You Are

**

• You enjoy building things from the ground up, and you are comfortable when not everything is defined yet

• You take ownership and follow through

• You can think big picture and still roll up your sleeves to fix a workflow yourself

• You explain data clearly, whether you are talking to a sales rep or to the leadership team

• You like working with people from many countries and cultures

**Benefits

**It is important for us to create a healthy, diverse, fun, and creative working environment, so besides all the basic benefits, we also focus a lot on social activities, flexible working hours and a good work life balance.

• Flexible Work Environment: Enjoy a collaborative, inclusive, and open workplace designed to fit your needs and support work-life balance.

• Competitive Package: A competitive salary, an 11% company pension plan, and a comprehensive benefits package.

• Time to Recharge: Benefit from 32 paid vacation days and paid parental leave to focus on what matters most.

• Career Growth: Access professional development opportunities and grow your career in a high-impact, high-growth industry.

• Stay Energized: Enjoy excellent coffee, tea, free snacks, and subsidized lunches at the office.

• Stay Active: Use our Spirii gym and shared company car to keep moving.

• Make an Impact: Be part of a team driving the future of sustainable energy while working on meaningful projects.

The position is a permanent position in Copenhagen, Denmark. Danish language is not a requirement, but Fluent English language skills are required.

**About Spirii – Who We Are

**Spirii is a full-service e-mobility provider which offers hardware and software charging solutions to companies in the private and the public sector. Spirii was founded seven years ago as a company. Nevertheless, the people in Spirii have extensive experience working with electric cars and charging, as well as the development of future transport- and energy systems.

Spirii is an equal opportunity employer. We encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds and experiences. Spirii strives to create an inclusive and diverse workplace, and we encourage all qualified applicants to apply regardless of age, gender, race, sexual/religious orientation, or disability.

Please note: This is a full-time office-based role (5 days/week)

About the role

We are looking for a Senior Newbuilding Manager to take commercial ownership of complex newbuilding and vessel investment projects across their full lifecycle, from initial business case and market engagement through contracting, construction and delivery.

This is a senior commercial role requiring strong judgement, negotiation capability and the ability to navigate high-value, complex investment decisions in a global environment. You will work closely with Fleet Technology, Network Strategy, Chartering, Vessel Portfolio Management, Finance, Treasury, Legal and other key functions to ensure projects deliver the right balance of commercial value, contractual protection, technical requirements and long-term value.

Beyond individual newbuilding projects, you will provide senior commercial capacity across the wider tonnage agenda, supporting transactions such as sale and purchase (SnP), purchase options, sale and leaseback arrangements, newbuild for time charter and contract amendments.

Key responsibilities

• Drive the commercial development, procurement and execution of assigned newbuilding and vessel investment projects, from business case through tendering, contracting, construction and delivery.

• Lead or contribute to investment business cases covering vessel specification, timing, commercial structure, risk, CAPEX, cash flows and total cost of ownership.

• Lead or support shipyard engagements, tender processes, bid evaluations and negotiations of Letters of Intent (LOIs) and Shipbuilding Contracts, in close collaboration with Legal, Fleet Technology and Finance.

• Lead commercial yard due diligence and counterparty assessments, including financial strength, risk and compliance, together with Finance, Treasury and Compliance.

• Act as the commercial contract owner throughout the project lifecycle, managing contractual milestones, payments, guarantees, options, claims and amendments.

• Coordinate cross-functional project teams and ensure high-quality, timely governance submissions, decision papers and management reporting.

• Provide flexible senior commercial capacity across the wider tonnage portfolio during peak periods, including SnP transactions, purchase options, sale and leaseback projects, newbuild for time charter and contractual amendments.

• Monitor shipyard capacity, pricing, market dynamics and competitor activity, translating market intelligence into actionable commercial analysis and recommendations.

• Build and maintain strong relationships with key shipyards, shipbrokers, OEMs, advisers and internal stakeholders.

• Contribute to consistent commercial processes, knowledge sharing and lessons learned across the Newbuilding team.

• Work closely with fellow Senior Newbuilding Managers, providing support and project coverage as portfolio priorities and workloads evolve.

• Identify and escalate material commercial exposures and decisions outside agreed mandate to the Head of Newbuilding, while maintaining ownership and momentum of agreed workstreams through completion.

Who we are looking for

You are a commercially strong shipping professional who can combine strategic thinking with hands-on execution. You are comfortable taking ownership of significant commercial commitments, challenging assumptions and navigating complex negotiations involving multiple internal and external stakeholders.

You bring:

• Significant commercial experience within shipping, vessel investment, newbuilding, sale and purchase, or a comparable capital-intensive industry.

• Proven experience leading complex commercial negotiations and managing high-value contractual commitments within defined mandates.

• Strong commercial judgement and the ability to balance price, vessel specification, delivery schedule, contractual risk and long-term value.

• Experience developing investment cases and translating complex commercial considerations into clear recommendations for senior management.

• A strong track record in tendering and contracting, combined with a solid understanding of key financial indicators including CAPEX, cash flows and total cost of ownership.

• The ability to manage several complex projects simultaneously and respond effectively to changing priorities and periods of high workload.

• Strong stakeholder management skills and experience working across multiple functions in a global, matrix organisation.

• Excellent communication skills, with the ability to influence and engage confidently at senior levels.

• A good understanding of vessel specifications and maritime technology.

• Experience working with Asian shipyards is considered a strong advantage.

• A high degree of ownership, commercial integrity and attention to detail.

What success looks like

Success in this role will be measured through:

• Commercial value and contractual protection secured across assigned investments and projects.

• Quality and timeliness of investment recommendations, decision papers and governance submissions.

• Delivery within approved cost, schedule, mandate and contractual parameters.

• Effective management of commercial risks, options, milestones and contractual deadlines.

• Ability to flex across projects and transactions as portfolio priorities change.

• Strength and quality of relationships with strategic shipyards and contribution to the continued development of the shipyard supply base.

You will play an important role in ensuring that major vessel investments are commercially robust, well governed and positioned to create long-term value, while strengthening our ability to engage strategically with the global shipyard market.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral researcher in quantitative genetics and genomics with a focus on inbreeding depression and genetic diversity management
jobs.employer_name: Center for Kvantitativ Genetik og Genomforskning
jobs.description:
The Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG) at Aarhus University, Denmark, invites applications for an exciting two-year postdoctoral position in the field of quantitative genetics and genomics applied to inbreeding management in livestock populations. The primary focus of this position is to investigate the genetic bases of inbreeding depression in dairy cattle.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a two-year position starting on 1 April 2027, or as soon as possible. 

Job description
This is an opportunity to integrate a top research environment and contribute to advancing the state of the art in inbreeding management, while working within a collaborative project involving key industry partners.

The overarching objective of the project is to quantify the impact of inbreeding depression load on economically important traits in dairy cattle breeds and to investigate whether recessive variants contributing to inbreeding depression segregate in genomic regions experiencing rapid accumulation of inbreeding. Particular attention will be given to regions surrounding monogenetic traits (e.g. polled locus, milk caseins) which have been subjected to strong selection pressure in recent years.

You will apply state-of-the-art quantitative genetic and genomic modelling approaches to evaluate the effect of inbreeding depression on a broad range of production and functional traits recorded in dairy cattle populations. To support these analyses, you will have access to extensive databases containing phenotypic records routinely collected on farm, as well as large-scale pedigree and SNP genomic datasets currently used in genomic evaluations. High-density SNP genotyping and whole-genome sequence data will also be available to search for causal variants and more finely describe the genetic architecture of inbreeding depression in dairy cattle. Ultimately, the project aims to incorporate these findings into practical mating software readily available to dairy farmers. Therefore, these activities will be carried out in close collaboration with industry partners to ensure practical implementation in the field. 

Within this position, the successful candidate will also have the opportunity to contribute to other research projects related to genetic diversity management and quantitative trait modelling across other livestock species. 

Your profile
• A Ph.D. in Quantitative Genetics, Population Genetics or similar.
• Good programming skills (R, Python or Julia)
• Experience in the use of software to estimate variance components is a plus (e.g. DMU, BLUPF90 or similar) 
• A team player and a good communicator
• A good track record of publication in international peer-reviewed journals

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in causality and machine learning for treatment decisions, jointly at the Pioneer Centre for AI and the Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed

jobs.description:
Department of Mathematical Sciences, Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen  The Department of Mathematical Sciences (MATH) invites applications for a PhD fellowship in causality and machine learning for treatment decisions. The fellowship is shared between the Pioneer Centre for AI and the Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed and is advertised at the Faculty of Science together with a three-year assistant professor position in causal inference at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences.

  The start date is 1 April 2027 or as soon as possible.  We are willing to accommodate the successful candidate’s situation, and the exact date is a matter of agreement.

  The setup: one project, two centres  You will be supervised by Sebastian Weichwald (Associate Professor at MATH, Copenhagen Causality Lab, and causality co-lead at the Pioneer Centre for AI) and Erin Gabriel (Professor at the Department of Public Health, causality theme lead and co-director of SMARTBiomed), and work closely with the assistant professor hired at Public Health also working jointly at the two centers, so that the link between the centres runs through daily work, not only meetings.

  Causal inference is a theme both centres share and approach from two sides. This position is for someone who wants both.

  About the centres: The Pioneer Centre for AI (https://www.aicentre.dk/), hosted by the Department of Computer Science with partners across Danish universities, does fundamental AI research. The Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed (https://smartbiomed.dk/) develops statistical and computational methods for large-scale biomedical data to improve the treatment and prevention of disease.

  The project  In diabetes management, continuous glucose monitoring is a high-frequency biomarker that is often used in treatment decisions. Given the huge amount of information summaries must be used; differences in summaries can lead to different decisions from the same raw data.  Treatment and prevention decisions increasingly rest on high-dimensional or high-frequency patient data such as biomarkers, wearable-device streams, omics profiles and longitudinal health records. In practice these are reduced to scores, coarser summaries, learned representations or patient states before a decision is made. The project asks when such a reduced representation still supports choosing between interventions, what is lost when it does not, and how representations can be learned with the decision in mind. It starts with the decision and works backwards to the measurements, transformations and assumptions that decision needs. This project aims to answer some of these questions in general, and to provide specific solutions In diabetes management.

  Who are we looking for?  The key requirement is competence: a master’s-level background with a high level of mathematical and computational training, for example from studies in statistics, mathematics, computer science or a nearby field, and an interest in causal inference. You should be interested in biomedical applications, ideally with some prior exposure through a thesis, a project, an internship or a collaboration, and willing to talk to and learn from clinicians and biomedical researchers about the context in which the methods will be used. Programming skills and willingness to turn methods into reusable software are expected.

   

  About the department

  The department has about 50 permanent scientific staff members, around 60 PhD students and 35 postdocs. It has strong research groups in many areas of mathematics and active PhD, postdoc, and visitors’ programs. Our buildings are located in central Copenhagen next to the central park Fælledparken. Our website https://www.math.ku.dk/english provides more information about the department and the research conducted at the department https://www.math.ku.dk/english/research/. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment.

  The PhD programme

  Depending on your level of education, you can undertake the PhD programme as either:

  Option A: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree.

  Option B: An up to five year full-time study programme within the framework of the integrated MSc and PhD programme (the 3+5 scheme), if you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree – but you have an education equivalent to a Danish bachelors´s degree.

   Option A: Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. statistics, mathematics, or computer science. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment in the regular programme Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant with the help of the supervisor.

  Terms of appointment and payment according to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Option B: Getting into a position on the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  If you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree, you might be qualified for the integrated MSc and PhD programme, if you have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish bachelor´s degree. Here you can find out, if that is relevant for you: General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of the integrated programme

  To be eligible for the integrated scholarship, you are (or are eligible to be) enrolled at one of the faculty’s master programmes.

  Students on the integrated programme will enroll as PhD students simultaneously with completing their enrollment in this MSc degree programme.

  The duration of the integrated programme is up to five years and depends on the amount of credits that you have passed on your MSc programme. For further information about the study programme, please see: www.science.ku.dk/phd, “Study Structures”.

  Until the MSc degree is obtained (when exactly two years of the full 3+5 programme remains), the grant will be paid partly in the form of up to 48 state education grant portions (in Danish: “SU-klip”) plus salary for work (teaching, supervision etc.) totalling a workload of 150 working hours per year. A PhD grant portion is currently (2026) DKK 7.426 before tax.

  When you have obtained the MSc degree, you will transfer to the salary-earning part of the scholarship for a period of two years. At that point, the terms of employment and payment will be according to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

   Responsibilities and tasks:

   	
• Complete and pass the MSc education in accordance with the curriculum of the MSc programme (ONLY when you are attending the integrated MSc and PhD programme) 	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision 	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teach and carry out knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at internationally recognized journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project 	
• Take part in the activities of both Pioneer Centres and spend time in both research environments   We are looking for candidates with the following qualifications and experience:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project, in particular a strong foundation in probability, statistics and/or machine learning at advanced master’s level 	
• Interest in and some exposure to biomedical applications, and willingness to work with clinicians and biomedical researchers 	
• Evidence of research ability in any form: a master’s thesis, a project, an internship or open-source work counts as much as a preprint; prior publications are not required 	
• Programming skills and interest in producing reusable, open software 	
• A curious mind-set with a strong interest in Mathematics and its applications 	
• Good English skills   Application and Assessment Procedure

  Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include:

   	
• Motivation letter (approximately 1.5 pages)
 	Propose your own angle on the project and argue how it fits the two groups and the wider network, including the Pioneer Centre for AI and SMARTBiomed. Tell us why this joint setup: what you expect from working across both groups that you would not get from either side alone or from an industrial machine learning lab, and how your background prepares you for it, including any experience with biomedical or other applied collaborations. 	
• Curriculum vitae (max. two pages) including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position. 	
• About you (max. one page, in prose). Tell us about the thing you are most proud of. We do not mean grades or prizes, but something you made or worked out: a report that was never published, a tool, a result, a course or side project. Say what it is and why it matters to you. Use the rest of the page for anything else you want us to know: people you have worked with, circumstances we should take into account when reading your CV, or context that does not fit a CV. 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor or Master and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. • Design, implement and manage the group's balance sheet reconciliations, including building standardised templates and processes across multiple entities

• Prepare the monthly and year-end group consolidation, including intercompany eliminations, foreign currency translation and consolidated reporting packs

• Ensure the general ledger is supported by complete, reviewed and documented reconciliations in every period. While taking a hands-on approach to booking journals and ad hoc analysis

Tax & Trade Compliance

• Own end-to-end packaging tax obligations, including data capture, calculation and filing

• Perform compliance reviews over packaging tax, taking a proactive approach as Tekla's global footprint grows

• Analyse customs and import duties, covering tariff classification, country of origin, preferential rates and duty paid versus duty due, and identify recovery and savings opportunities.

Financial Analysis & Performance

• Monitor cash flow, working capital, and financial performance metrics

• Perform variance and accuracy analyses to validate forecasts, budgets, and data integrity, encouraging transparency and accountability

• Investigate material variances and implement process improvements that enhance forecasting precision and analytical rigour

• Provide insightful financial analysis to support business planning, cost efficiencies and strategic priorities

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to support business objectives

Process Improvement & Automation

• Drive continuous improvement by leveraging AI and emerging technologies to enhance financial processes, systems, and reporting tools

• Support the automation programme within the accounting team, including Intrastat and VAT reporting

• Review and implement continual improvements in Business Central, including VAT code configuration, VAT statements and financial reports

• Strengthen documentation and controls across all owned processes so they are auditable and transferable
